1.word_for_word: ऊनषष्टितमे भौमं हत्वा तेनाहृता हरिः । — In the sixty-ninth year, Lord Hari killed Bhūma and took him away.; कन्याः सहस्रशः प्राप पारिजातं दिवोऽहरत् ॥ — He obtained thousands of daughters and took away the pārijāta tree from heaven.; परिणीय ततस् ताभिस् तन्-मनोरथ-पूरणैः । — Then he married her and fulfilled her desires.; आत्मारामो\ऽप्य् असौ रेमे तद्-गृहेषु गृहस्थवत् ॥ — Although he was self-satisfied, he enjoyed his homes like a householder.; येन ताः स्त्रियो निरुद्धाः स भौमः । — The one who stopped those women was Bhauma.; च-काराद् येन कारणेन हतस् तद् आचक्ष्वेति ॥१॥ — Tell me the reason why he was killed by the f-kara.
1.translation: In the sixty-ninth year, Lord Hari killed Bhūma and took him away. He obtained thousands of daughters and took away the pārijāta tree from heaven. Then he married her and fulfilled her desires. Although he was self-satisfied, he enjoyed his homes like a householder. The one who stopped those women was Bhauma. Tell me the reason why he was killed by the f-kara.

2.word_for_word: इन्द्रेण भौम-विचेष्टितं ज्ञापितः सन् प्राग्ज्योतिष-पुरं भौम-नगरं ययाव् इत्य् अन्वयः । — The consequence is that when Indra informed him of Bhouma’s movements, he went to the city of Bhouma, the city of Pragjyotish.; किं-भूतेन ? — What-by-the-ghost?; हृतं छत्रं यस्य तेन । — He whose umbrella has been taken away.; लोकपाल-प्रधानत्वाद् इन्द्रस्य वरुण-च्छत्र-हरणेऽपि तस्यैव मान-भङ्ग इति तथोक्तम् । — Because Indra is the chief guardian of the worlds, it is said that even when Indra took away Varuna’s umbrella, it was a violation of his dignity.; हृते कुण्डले यस्याः सा अदितिर् बन्धुर् माता यस्य तेन । — The woman whose earrings were taken away was Aditi, the friend of the man whose mother was taken away.; हृतम् अमराद्रौ स्थानं मणिपर्वत-लक्षणं यस्य तेन । — He took away the place on the mountain of Amara, which is characterized by the mountain of gems.; सत्यभामाया गृहे भगवन्तम् इन्द्र आगत्य विज्ञापितवांस् तदा तस्याः कौतुकाय तया भार्यया सह ययाव् इति । — Indra came to the house of Satyabhāmā and informed her that he had gone with his wife to curiosity her.; यद् वा, \"त्वद्-अनुज्ञयैव त्वत्-पुत्रं हनिष्यामि\" इतीतिहासोक्तं भूम्यै वरं दत्तं सत्यं कर्तुं सत्यभामाया भूम्यंशत्वात् तया सह ययौ । — Or rather, to fulfill the boon given to the earth as stated in history, \"I shall kill your son with your permission,\" he went with Satyabhāmā, who was part of the earth.; यद् वा, नारदानीत-पारिजातैक-कुसुमे रुक्मिण्यै दत्ते सति कुपितां सत्यभामां सान्त्वयता \"तुभ्यं पारिजातम् एव दास्यामि\" इति श्री-कृष्णेन प्रतिश्रुतम् इति हरि-वंशे प्रसिद्धं तद्-अर्थं तां नीतवान् इति ॥२॥ — Or that it is well known in the Hari dynasty that when Lord Kṛṣṇa consoled the angry Satyabhāmā when He gave her a single parijata flower brought by Nārada to Rukmiṇī, he promised her, "I shall give you only the parijata flower.
2.translation: The consequence is that when Indra informed him of Bhouma’s movements, he went to the city of Bhouma, the city of Pragjyotish. What-by-the-ghost? He whose umbrella has been taken away. Because Indra is the chief guardian of the worlds, it is said that even when Indra took away Varuna’s umbrella, it was a violation of his dignity. The woman whose earrings were taken away was Aditi, the friend of the man whose mother was taken away. He took away the place on the mountain of Amara, which is characterized by the mountain of gems. Indra came to the house of Satyabhāmā and informed her that he had gone with his wife to curiosity her. Or rather, to fulfill the boon given to the earth as stated in history, \"I shall kill your son with your permission,\" he went with Satyabhāmā, who was part of the earth. Or that it is well known in the Hari dynasty that when Lord Kṛṣṇa consoled the angry Satyabhāmā when He gave her a single parijata flower brought by Nārada to Rukmiṇī, he promised her, "I shall give you only the parijata flower.

3-4.word_for_word: गरुडेन याने कारणम्, गिरि-दुर्गैर् इत्य्-आदि । — The reason for the eagle in the chariot, the mountains and fortresses, and so on.; तैर् उपलक्षितम् । — They have observed.; जलाग्न्य्-अनिलैश् च सर्वतो वर्तमानैर् दुर्गमम् ॥ — It is difficult to reach because of the water, fire and wind that are present everywhere.; ३-४ ॥ — 3-4
3-4.translation: The reason for the eagle in the chariot, the mountains and fortresses, and so on. They have observed. It is difficult to reach because of the water, fire and wind that are present everywhere. 3-4

5-6.word_for_word: युगान्ताशनेर् ध्वनिवद् भीषणम् । — It was as terrifying as the sound of the end of the age.; परिखाया जलात् ॥६-७॥ — from the water of the moat.6-7
5-6.translation: It was as terrifying as the sound of the end of the age. from the water of the moat.6-7

8.word_for_word: आविध्य आतोल्य स महान् नाद इत्य् अन्वयः ॥८॥ — That great sound, which was rolled and shaken, is the consequence.
8.translation: That great sound, which was rolled and shaken, is the consequence.

9.word_for_word: तस्मै श्री-कृष्णाय गदां व्यमुञ्चत व्यक्षिपत् ॥९-१०॥ — He released his club and threw it at that Lord Krishna (9-10).
9.translation: He released his club and threw it at that Lord Krishna (9-10).

11.word_for_word: इन्द्र-तेजसा वज्रेण । — By the thunderbolt of Indra’s effulgence.; प्रतिक्रियया हेतु-भूतया अमर्ष-जुषः ॥११॥ — He is enraged by the cause-and-effect reaction.
11.translation: By the thunderbolt of Indra’s effulgence. He is enraged by the cause-and-effect reaction.

12.word_for_word: पीठं पीठ-नामानम् । — The seat is called the seat.; निरगन् निरगमन् ॥१२॥ — They went out and went out.
12.translation: The seat is called the seat. They went out and went out.

14.word_for_word: कृत्तानि शीर्षादीनि येषां तान् ॥१४॥ — Those whose heads and other parts have been cut off.
14.translation: Those whose heads and other parts have been cut off.

15.word_for_word: शतघ्नीं शक्ति-विशेषम् ॥१५॥ — Shataghnīm is a special power.

16.word_for_word: विचित्रा वाजाः पत्राणि येषां तैर् बाणैर् निकृत्ता बाहव ऊरवः शिरोध्राः कन्धरा विग्रहा देहाश् च यस्मिंस् तत् । — The arms, thighs, necks, shoulders, and bodies of the dead were cut off by the arrows of the demigods, whose leaves were of various kinds.; तर्ह्य् एव तं यदा विव्यधुस्तस्मिन्न् एव क्षणे ॥१६॥ — That very moment when they pierced him
16.translation: The arms, thighs, necks, shoulders, and bodies of the dead were cut off by the arrows of the demigods, whose leaves were of various kinds. That very moment when they pierced him

17-19.word_for_word: अत्याश्चर्ये कुरूद्वहेति सम्बोधनम् । — In a very surprising way, he was addressed as Kurudvaha.; तथा हि, तैर् यानि प्रयुक्तानि शस्त्रास्त्राणि तत्प्राप्तेः पूर्वम् एव तत्सर्वं सैन्यं हत्वा पश्चात्तानि शस्त्राण्यस्त्राणि च चिच्छेद । — Thus, before they could get the weapons they used, he killed all the army and cut off the weapons and armor that followed.; तत्राप्य् एकैकं शस्त्रम् अस्त्रं च त्रिभिः शरैर् इत्याश्चर्यम् । — It is also surprising that each weapon is fired by three arrows; किं च, गरुत्मतेति ॥१७-१९॥ — What is more, Garutmata.17-1
17-19.translation: In a very surprising way, he was addressed as Kurudvaha. Thus, before they could get the weapons they used, he killed all the army and cut off the weapons and armor that followed. It is also surprising that each weapon is fired by three arrows What is more, Garutmata.17-1

20.word_for_word: यतो यया शक्त्या वज्रः प्रतिहत आस । — Because of the force with which the thunderbolt was repulsed.; गरुडस् तु नाकम्पत ॥२०॥ — Garuda, however, did not tremble.
20.translation: Because of the force with which the thunderbolt was repulsed. Garuda, however, did not tremble.

21.word_for_word: गरुडे वितथोद्यमः सन् शूलं त्रिशूलम् आददे धृतवान् ॥२१-२२॥ — Having failed in his attempt at Garuda he took up the trident and held it in his hands (21-22).
21.translation: Having failed in his attempt at Garuda he took up the trident and held it in his hands (21-22).

23.word_for_word: प्रतप्ते जाम्बूनदे यानि रत्नानि तैर् भास्वरे । — The jewels in the burning golden river shone brightly.; मेर्व्-अंश-भूतं मन्दर-शिखरं महा-मणिं चार्पयद् इति ॥२३-२४॥ — He offered the peak of Mandara which was a part of Merva and the great jewel (23-24).
23.translation: The jewels in the burning golden river shone brightly. He offered the peak of Mandara which was a part of Merva and the great jewel (23-24).

25.word_for_word: ऐश्वर्यं ज्ञात्वा भूमिः स्तौति । — Knowing the wealth, the earth praises it.; नमस्त इति । — Hello, it’s.; परमात्मन् देवाद्यन्तर्यामिन् ॥२५॥ — O Supreme Soul, in the midst of the gods.
25.translation: Knowing the wealth, the earth praises it. Hello, it’s. O Supreme Soul, in the midst of the gods.

26.word_for_word: येन मन्त्रेण कुन्त्याः प्रसन्नः पूर्वमासीत्, तेन मन्त्रेण नमस्यति---नम इति । — He will bow down to her with the mantra by which he was pleased with Kunti in the past.; पङ्कजं नाभौ यस्य, तस्मै जगत्कारणायेत्य् अर्थः । — The lotus in his navel means that he is the cause of the universe.; अत एव सत्कीर्तिमयी पङ्कजमाला विद्यते गस्य तस्मै । — That is why the cow has a garland of lotuses full of good fame.; एवंभूतं ध्यायतां पङ्कजवत्सुप्रसन्ने तापोपशमने नेत्रे यस्य तस्मै । — Please meditate on the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose eyes are like lotus flowers, which are very happy and relieve suffering.; पङ्कजवत्सुसेव्यौ पङ्कजाङ्कितौ वाङ्घ्री यस्य तस्मै नम इति ॥२६॥ — I offer my obeisances to Him whose feet are marked with lotuses and are well-served like lotuses.
26.translation: He will bow down to her with the mantra by which he was pleased with Kunti in the past. The lotus in his navel means that he is the cause of the universe. That is why the cow has a garland of lotuses full of good fame. Please meditate on the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose eyes are like lotus flowers, which are very happy and relieve suffering. I offer my obeisances to Him whose feet are marked with lotuses and are well-served like lotuses.

27-28.word_for_word: किं च, भगवते निरतिशयैश्वर्याय वासुदेवाय सर्व-भूताश्रयायात एव विष्णवे व्यापिने । — What is more, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, who is infinitely opulent, is the shelter of all living entities, and He is the all-pervading Lord Viṣṇu.; न हि सर्व-भूताश्रयत्वं परिच्छिन्नस्य सम्भवतीति कुतः सर्वाश्रयत्वं तत्राह---पुरुषाय सर्वस्मात्कार्यात् पूर्वम् एव सते, पूर्वम् एवाहमिहासम् इति तत्पुरुषस्य पुरुषत्वं इति श्रुतेः । — For it is not possible for a separated person to be dependent on all beings, so why should he be dependent on all things?; एतद् अपि कुतः । — Where is this, too?; आदिबीजाय । — Adibijaya.; आदेर्जगत्कारणस्यापि कारणाय । — For the cause of the universe in the beginning.; एवम् अपि न मृदादिवज्जाड्यम् इत्य् आह---पूर्णबोधायेति ॥२७॥ — Even so, it is not dull like clay and other things, he argues, for the sake of complete enlightenment.; नन्व् एवम् अपि स्वस्य कारणात् पूर्वं सत्त्वं न स्यादत आह---अजायेति । — If, however, there is no existence of existence before its own cause, he argues that it is unborn.; स्वयम् अजाय । — Ajay himself.; अस्य च जगतो जनयित्रे । — And to the originator of this universe.; उभयत्रापि क्रमेण हेतुद्वयम्, ब्रह्मणे बृहते, अनन्तशक्तय इति च । — In both cases, there are two causes in order, namely, the great Brahman and the infinite powers.; बृहत्त्वाद् अजत्वम्, अनन्तशक्तित्वात् तज्जनयितृत्वम् इत्य् अर्थः । — Because of its greatness, it is unborn, and because of its infinite power, it is the cause of it.; ननु पित्रादयः पुत्रादीनां जनकास्तेषां च तत्पूर्वे तेषां च भूतानि तेषां च स्वकर्मद्वारेण जीवाः किम् अत्राहं तत्राह---परावरात्मन्न् इत्य्-आदि । — If, indeed, fathers and others are the fathers of sons and others, and before them, and before them, and through their own actions, they are living beings.; पित्राद्यात्मकत्वात् त्वम् एव जनक इत्य् अर्थः ॥२८॥ — Being composed of fathers and others, it means that You alone are the father.
27-28.translation: What is more, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vāsudeva, who is infinitely opulent, is the shelter of all living entities, and He is the all-pervading Lord Viṣṇu. For it is not possible for a separated person to be dependent on all beings, so why should he be dependent on all things? Where is this, too? Adibijaya. For the cause of the universe in the beginning. Even so, it is not dull like clay and other things, he argues, for the sake of complete enlightenment. If, however, there is no existence of existence before its own cause, he argues that it is unborn. Ajay himself. And to the originator of this universe. In both cases, there are two causes in order, namely, the great Brahman and the infinite powers. Because of its greatness, it is unborn, and because of its infinite power, it is the cause of it. If, indeed, fathers and others are the fathers of sons and others, and before them, and before them, and through their own actions, they are living beings. Being composed of fathers and others, it means that You alone are the father.

29.word_for_word: ननु गुणा विश्वोत्पत्त्यादिहेतवस् ते च प्रधानस्य् एव तस्य च पुरुषः क्षोभकस् तत्र च कालो निमित्तम् इति प्रसिद्धं किमत्राहं तत्राह---त्वं वा इति । — Indeed, it is well known that the modes of nature are the causes of the creation of the universe and other things, and that they are the cause of the principal, and that the person is the disturber of it, and that time is the cause of it.; तमसो धारणे\ऽप्य् असंवृत एव । — Even in the hold of darkness, it is uncovered.; स्थानाय पालनाय । — to take care of the place.; जगतः सृष्ट्याद्यर्थमुत्कटं रजआदि त्वम् एव बिभर्षि सृजसीत्य् अर्थः । — This means that You alone carry and create the dust and other elements that are the cause of the creation of the universe.; कालप्रधानपुरुषाश् च त्वद्व्यतिरिक्ता न सन्ति त्वं तु परः सर्व-व्यतिरिक्तः । — There are no other beings besides You who are the chiefs of time but You are the Supreme Being beyond all others; अतस् त्वम् एव जनयितेत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥ — Therefore, it means that You alone are the cause.
29.translation: Indeed, it is well known that the modes of nature are the causes of the creation of the universe and other things, and that they are the cause of the principal, and that the person is the disturber of it, and that time is the cause of it. Even in the hold of darkness, it is uncovered. to take care of the place. This means that You alone carry and create the dust and other elements that are the cause of the creation of the universe. There are no other beings besides You who are the chiefs of time but You are the Supreme Being beyond all others Therefore, it means that You alone are the cause.

30.word_for_word: कार्य-कारणप्रपञ्चस्य तदव्यतिरेकं तस्य च सर्व-व्यतिरेकमुपपादयति । — It produces the distinction between the world of cause and effect and the distinction between it and all of it.; अहम् इति । — I’m the one.; अहं भूमिः । — I am the earth.; मात्राणीति देवा मन इन्द्रियाणीति च त्रिविधाहङ्कारकार्याणि । — The senses, the demigods, the mind and the senses are the threefold functions of the ego.; कर्ताऽहङ्कारः ॥३०॥ — The doer is the ego.
30.translation: It produces the distinction between the world of cause and effect and the distinction between it and all of it. I’m the one. I am the earth. The senses, the demigods, the mind and the senses are the threefold functions of the ego. The doer is the ego.

31.word_for_word: एवं स्तुत्वा प्रार्थयते, तस्येति । — Thus he praises and prays, saying, 'This is his.; हे प्रपन्नार्ति-हर ! — O Prapannarti-hara!; तस्य नरकस्य अयं भगदत्तो नाम भीतोऽत एव मया तव पादपङ्कजम् उपसादितः ॥३१॥ — This man named Bhagadatta is afraid of that hell and therefore I have come to Thy lotus feet.
31.translation: Thus he praises and prays, saying, 'This is his. O Prapannarti-hara! This man named Bhagadatta is afraid of that hell and therefore I have come to Thy lotus feet.

33.word_for_word:
शताधिकम् इत्य् अपि ज्ञातव्यम् । — It should also be noted that it is more than a hundred.; यथाह श्री-पराशरः, — As Sri-Parashara says,; > कन्या-पुरे स कन्यानां षोडशातुल-विक्रमः । — > In the city of girls, he was the sixteenth of the girls.; >
> शताधिकानि ददृशे सहस्राणि महामते ॥ — >
> O great soul he saw more than a hundred thousand; [वि।पु। — [V.P.; ५.२९.३१] इति । — 5.29.31] is used.; राजभ्य इत्य् उपलक्षणं सिद्धादिभ्यश् चेति । — The sub-characteristic is to the kings, and to the Siddhas and others.; तथा च तेनैवोक्तम्, — And so he said,; > देव-सिद्धासुरादीनां नृपाणां च जनार्दन । — > O Janārdana, among the demigods, Siddhas, asuras and other kings,; >
> हृत्वा हि सोऽसुरः कन्या रुरोध निज-मन्दिरे ॥ — >
> The demon took the girl and locked her in his temple.; [वि।पु। — [V.P.; ५.२९.९] > इति ॥३३-३५॥ — 5.29.9] > 33-3
33.translation:
It should also be noted that it is more than a hundred. As Sri-Parashara says, > In the city of girls, he was the sixteenth of the girls. >
